slide 5 ('Typical failure categories in agent traces'): [fact] The claim that empirical studies of AlphaCode and autonomous agents reveal exactly four dominant failure modes is unsupported and likely misleading, since AlphaCode is primarily a code-generation system rather than evidence for this specific four-category taxonomy. Fix: Say that the four categories are a practical taxonomy for this exercise, not a definitive result from AlphaCode studies. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

evidence.title: Typical failure categories in agent traces

findings.message: slide 6 ('Trace excerpt: a type error cascade'): [fact] The slide labels the excerpt as a type-error cascade and refers to a runtime TypeError, but the shown trace contains a TypeError followed by a ValueError and does not show the caller, input, or line references. Fix: Describe it as an input-coercion failure sequence and either include the caller/input evidence or remove the unsupported line-number claims. (rewritten to fix this; not re-read by the reviewer)

evidence.title: Trace excerpt: a type error cascade

findings.message: slide 6 ('Trace excerpt: a type error cascade'): [clarity] The bullets cite lines 12, 45, and 78, but the displayed JSONL has only four records and no line-number field, so students cannot map the bullets to the excerpt. Fix: Use record numbers that match the displayed excerpt or label the bullets as hypothetical locations in the full trace. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

evidence.title: Trace excerpt: a type error cascade

findings.message: slide 8 ('Toolchain for trace collection and querying'): [fact] The table implies that JSONL plus jq supports SQL queries, although jq is a JSON processor and does not provide SQL querying. Fix: List jq under JSONL filtering and list a separate SQL-capable tool for relational queries. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

evidence.title: Toolchain for trace collection and querying

findings.message: slide 8 ('Toolchain for trace collection and querying'): [fact] The table lists Grafana as the visualization tool for Parquet plus SQL, but Grafana is primarily a dashboard and visualization layer and does not itself query Parquet files. Fix: Name a Parquet-compatible query engine such as DuckDB and state that Grafana can visualize its exported query results. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

evidence.title: Toolchain for trace collection and querying

findings.message: slide 9 ('Check: trace analysis fundamentals'): [quiz] The question asks which log element most directly reveals a specification mismatch, but both the prompt text and the diff between expected and actual output can provide direct evidence of such a mismatch. Fix: Ask which element most directly compares required behavior with observed behavior, or make the prompt-text option explicitly insufficient by stating that it contains only the task description. (rewritten to fix this; not re-read by the reviewer)

slide 15 ('Reliability metrics for software factories'): [other] The targets of greater than 90 percent, less than 30 minutes, and a balanced failure-type distribution are presented as universal targets without a stated basis. Fix: Label these as illustrative team targets to be set from project context rather than standard requirements. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

slide 16 ('Closing the loop: trace‑driven model improvement'): [fact] The claim that this mirrors the AlphaCode approach of using execution outcomes as reward signals misstates AlphaCode, which used large-scale sampling and filtering for code generation rather than this trace-driven fine-tuning and reward-model loop. Fix: Remove the AlphaCode comparison or describe it accurately as an example of execution-based filtering for generated programs. (rewritten to fix this; not re-read by the reviewer)

evidence.title: Closing the loop: trace‑driven model improvement

findings.message: slide 16 ('Closing the loop: trace‑driven model improvement'): [fact] The slide presents trace-derived fine-tuning and reward modeling as a direct consequence of trace analysis without noting that successful execution alone does not establish correctness or provide a reliable training signal. Fix: State that traces must be curated and independently validated before use as training or reward data. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)

evidence.title: Closing the loop: trace‑driven model improvement

findings.message: slide 17 ('Key takeaways'): [fact] The takeaway that testing must be independent of the generator is too absolute because independently generated tests can still share the generator's blind spots. Fix: Say that validation should use diverse and independently validated tests, including human-authored or property-based checks. (found before the rewrite; the slide may have moved)
